Assume \textup{(K1)}. The category $\A(M,G,\K)$ is exact over $R$ if and only if the functor of coinvariants preserves monomorphisms of smooth $R[G]$-modules. Equivalently: in the topos of continuous $G$-sets, the left adjoint of the functor that gives an $R$-module the trivial action of $G$ is exact on $R$-module objects. In particular exactness over $R$ depends only on this topos.

Assume \textup{(K1)}. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ with finitely many orbits on $G/G_B$ for every $B\in\K$, and let $k$ be a ring such that coinvariants preserve monomorphisms of smooth $k[H]$-modules (smooth for $H$: every element is fixed by $H\cap G_B$ for some finite $B$). For $B\in\K$ let $E(B)=G_B\backslash G/H$. \begin{itemize} \item[\textup{(a)}] If there are functions $\mu_B\colon E(B)\to k$, $B\in\K$, of total sum $1$, compatible with the restriction maps $E(C)\to E(B)$ for $B\subseteq C$ and with the action of $G$ \textup{(}a \emph{normalized invariant measure}, Definition~\textup{\ref{def:measure})}, then $\A(M,G,\K)$ is exact over every $k$-algebra. \item[\textup{(b)}] If $k$ is a field and $\A(M,G,\K)$ is exact over $k$, there is such a family. \item[\textup{(c)}] If $G$ is amenable and $k\supseteq\Q$, there is such a family; so $\A(M,G,\K)$ is then exact over every $\Q$-algebra. \end{itemize}

Let $\Po$ be the class of finite structures $(P,\prec,<)$, where $\prec$ is a strict partial order and $<$ a linear order on $P$, let $M_{\Po}$ be its Fra\"iss\'e limit and $G=\Aut(M_{\Po})$. The category of non-empty members of $\Po$ and embeddings is exact over every ring. The group $G$ is not amenable \textup{(}Kechris and Soki\'c \cite[Remark~3.2]{KS}\textup{)}.

Let $\V$ be the category of finite-dimensional non-zero vector spaces over $\F_2$ with a linear order on the set of their non-zero vectors, and of injective linear maps that preserve the order. Let $(V_\infty,<)$ be its Fra\"iss\'e limit and $G$ the group of linear automorphisms of $V_\infty$ that preserve the order. \begin{itemize} \item[\textup{(a)}] $G$ is amenable. \item[\textup{(b)}] $\V$ is exact over every $\Q$-algebra. \item[\textup{(c)}] $\V$ is not exact over any ring in which $2$ is not invertible; in particular not over $\F_2$ and not over $\Z$. \end{itemize}

Let $M=M_{\Po}$, $G=\Aut(M)$, let $W$ be a set with an action of $G$ in which every point has an open stabilizer, $R$ a ring, $Y$ an $R[G]$-submodule of the free module $R[W]$, and $x\in R[W]$. Let $U$ be an open subgroup of $G$ fixing $x$, and $\Omega_U\colon R[W]\to R[U\backslash W]$ the map that sends a point to its $U$-orbit. Then $x\in Y$ if and only if $\Omega_U(x)\in\Omega_U(Y)$. If $R$ is a field and $x\notin Y$, there is a $U$-invariant function $f\colon W\to R$ whose linear extension vanishes on $Y$ and not on $x$.
If coinvariants preserve monomorphisms of smooth $R[G]$-modules, the same holds for every open subgroup $U$ of $G$. Then for every smooth $R[U]$-module $N$ the map $N^U\to N_U$ is injective.
The category $\A$ is exact over $R$ if and only if every finite family of arrows $a_0,\dots,a_k\colon P\to Q$ of $\A$ has an affine equalizer over $R$.
In a category with finite sets of arrows and the Ramsey property, every finite family $a_0,\dots,a_k\colon P\to Q$ has an affine equalizer over $\Z$, and property \textup{(Re)} holds.
Assume \textup{(K1)}. If $\A(M,G,\K)$ has property \textup{(Re)}, then $G$ is amenable.

The integers $w_P(\pi)$ are invariant under isomorphisms of structures $(P,\prec,<)$, their sum over the linear extensions of $P$ is $1$, and for every subset $Q\subseteq P$, with the induced relations, and every linear extension $\tau$ of $Q$, \[ \sum_{\pi|_Q=\tau}w_P(\pi)=w_Q(\tau). \]
The category $\C$ has the Ramsey property, and it is exact over $\Z$.
